- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., < 0.33) and supply net is large negative, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior), model often overshoots and fails to adjust — apply downward drag or lagged smoothing to prevent overreaction.
- In high-event periods (e.g., >15 events/30d, net supply negative), model underestimates downside risk — increase downward bias or add volatility penalty to forecast.
- When bullish sentiment is low but supply is negative, model often ignores bearish pressure — adjust forecast downward by 5–10% of recent mean if sentiment < 0.67.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment shifts in early days of event cycles — if sentiment flips from bullish to bearish within 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 2–5% per day.
- In multi-event windows (e.g., 3+ auctions in 7 days), model often fails to account for cumulative supply shock — apply exponential decay to event impact or use rolling average of recent supply net.
